Messages.Author: Joe Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <3b2vp0$2...@news.acns.nwu.edu>,


The card is played during combat (when it's not your turn) on a vampire
who is about to *deal* aggravated damage. That vampire is pretty much
hosed for a while. It's best used against a deck that has vampires that
like to deal aggravated damage.

Actually, I thought it was used on a vampire that would be

Here's what the card says:

MASTER: OUT OF TURN
Play when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage against a
vampire, whether successfully or not. Combat ends before damage
is resolved. That vampire is put in torpor, tapped, with this
card on it. During the vampire's next untap phase, burn this
card instread [sic] of untapping the vampire.

From this, the card is played on the vampire... i.e. the
entity being damaged in the first setence.
Keep in mind, that aggravated damage that removes all the blood
from a vampire and then some BURNS the vampire after the round
is resolved, where normal damage that removes all the blood
from a vampire and then some sends it to torpor. (Can someone
confirm this?)

Rotschreck seems to be a card that protects vampires that are
about to be burned.
However, I can see this used as a weapon to keep a vampire in
torpor for a couple of rounds.

I could be wrong, and I probably am. If I am wrong, then the
card is poorly worded.

Messages.Author: Joe Cochran
Messages.Body:
In article <brianm.7...@wopr.gsm.uci.edu>,

Brian MacDonald <bri...@wopr.gsm.uci.edu> wrote:
> Keep in mind, that aggravated damage that removes all the blood
> from a vampire and then some BURNS the vampire after the round
> is resolved, where normal damage that removes all the blood
> from a vampire and then some sends it to torpor. (Can someone
> confirm this?)
>

Aggravated damage send the vampire to torpor immediately. The first
point of aggravated damage doesn't even remove a blood, it's the torpor
shot. The only time a vampire is immediately burned is when there's
more than one point of aggravated damage and the vampire doesn't have
the blood to compensate for it all. It doesn't remove all of the blood
unless you do N+1 points where N is the number of blood on the vampire
you're hitting with the damage. And to burn the vampire, you have to
do N+2 in aggravated points.

Messages.Author: Owen Reynolds
Messages.Body:
>>> Could anyone give me a clarification of how the Rotschreck card is
>>>played/when it is used?
>>>thanks in advance

In the game Vampire:The Masquarade, the word Rotschreck means more-or-
less "incontrollable fear" and is brought on by certain things like fire
or the prospect of suffering unhealable damage (which is the reason to
fear fire, as well.)
In the game, 99% of the time Rotschreck affects a vampire facing some
horrible fate, causing said vampire to berserkly jump out windows and run
at 30mph for 6 blocks. The other 1% of the time, a vampire will be trying
to use a flamethrower as a weapon and will get frightened as (s)he turns
it on.

I quote a previous poster who explains how the card's wording says
the same thing (it affects a vampire about to receive damage):

> Actually, I thought it was used on a vampire that would be
> *DEALT* aggravated damage.

> Here's what the card says:
>
> MASTER: OUT OF TURN
> Play when a minion attempts to use aggravated damage against a
> vampire, whether successfully or not. Combat ends before damage
> is resolved. That vampire is put in torpor, tapped, with this
> card on it. During the vampire's next untap phase, burn this
> card instread [sic] of untapping the vampire.

> Keep in mind, that aggravated damage that removes all the blood
> from a vampire and then some BURNS the vampire after the round
> is resolved, where normal damage that removes all the blood
> from a vampire and then some sends it to torpor. (Can someone
> confirm this?)

Yes, but you have to be careful. The first point of aggravated damage
sends it to torpor, the rest splash blood around and any extra destroy the
victim. It's easy to think a 3-blood vampire is killed by a 4-point
aggravated strike, but it takes 5.

> Rotschreck seems to be a card that protects vampires that are
> about to be burned.

Played as written, it's a way to prevent anyone from getting away
from your claws. A claw strike puts the victim in torpor, whereas Rotschreck
puts them in torpor for an extra turn, so it's not a bad weapon.
It's best use is when the victim has armour, fortitude and/or a
dangerous HtH attack. Rotschreck negates the armour and the fortitude
and saves your vampire from taking the nasty strike, making it amazingly
effective in the right circumstances.

The design team ruling has got me completely confused (that Rotschreck
affects the vampire about to _deal_ the damage.) There are already lots
of ways around aggravated damage -- maneuvers are easiest since most
agg. damage is from claws; Fortitude works fine; weapons are expensive and
can be stolen or burned (like Flamethrowers.) Agg. damage isn't really
all that bad, even, for what you pay to be able to do it.
There's no V:tM rational why it would work that way. It's like having
a card named "find lots of money" that made a vampire lose 2 blood and
the explaination, "someone else finds lots of that vampire's money."

When first playing it, I played it that way. Here's the two points
that changed my mind. (Niether are WotC rulings as I'm still waiting for
them to make up their mind and publish something that isn't retracted
immediatly.)

1) From a Vamp: the Masqurade playing friend, Rotschreck is apparently
a massive fear, especially of sunlight or fire, i.e. stuff that does
aggrivated damage. Hence, the argument is that the *victim* runs away for
a long time and can't be controlled for a long while (2 turns as the card
reads). This is week as game mechanics frequently have nothing to do with
the sourses the game is based on.

2) The card text. It is admittedly obscure but here's what it says:
"Play when a minion attempts to use aggrivated damage against a vampire,
whether successfully or not. Combat ends before damage is resolved. The

vampire is put in torpor, tapped, with this card on it. During the

vampire's next untap phase, burn this card instead of untapping the vampire."

Note that, in the first sentence, the *dealer* of the damage is
refered to as a _minion_, whereas the *victim* is refered to as a
_vampire_. Also note, that further on, when describing what happens to
whoever it is that gets hosed by this card, it always describes the one
getting hosed as _the vampire_, thus the *victim* from the first sentence.

Secondly on this point is that this card could be played if my
Slashers, armed with a Flamethrower, attacked, say, Brazil. If the dealer
is supposed to get hosed, that would mean the Slashers would have to go
to torpor! This, of course, can't happen, my Slashers are mortal.

Thus, my mind is pretty much made up. Unless there is serious errata
to this card, I say the *victim* gets hosed. Any counter arguments?

Don Sowell
